Value Chain Analysis

The Communications Platform as a Service (“CPaaS”) industry value chain comprises a sequence of interconnected software
development, platform orchestration, and service delivery activities spanning platform conceptualization, enterprise-scale
deployment, and lifecycle management. Each stage contributes to value creation, scalability, compliance assurance, cost
structure, and margin profile, shaped by technological capabilities, regulatory frameworks, enterprise requirements, and global
carrier connectivity.




                      Platform                              Service                              Post-           End-User
    Opportunity                          Carrier &                          Execution,
                    Development                           Deployment                          Deployment        Engagement
   Identification                         Partner                          Monitoring &
                        & API                             & Campaign                           Support &        & Feedback
   & Solutioning                        Onboarding                           Analytics
                    Deployment                           Configuration                        Optimization         Loop




1. Opportunity Identification & Solutioning

   The value chain begins with market and client opportunity assessment. CPaaS providers engage in enterprise outreach,
   developer community engagement, and feasibility evaluation of integration requirements. Solutioning includes defining
   required communication channels (messaging, voice, video, email), workflow automation, regulatory compliance
   (DLT/TRAI, GDPR), and integration complexity with enterprise systems (CRM, ERP). Success at this stage depends on
   understanding client workflows, regulatory mandates, platform capabilities, and competitive differentiation. This stage shapes
   contract scope, revenue potential, and risk allocation.

2. Platform Development & API Deployment

   Core value creation occurs through designing and deploying programmable APIs, SDKs, and omnichannel orchestration
   tools. Activities include platform architecture design, cloud infrastructure provisioning, multi-channel message routing,
   AI/ML conversational models, and developer portal creation. Integration with enterprise applications, CRM/ERP systems,
   and cloud ecosystems is performed here. Efficient development ensures platform reliability, scalability, low latency, and
   adherence to data protection and regulatory frameworks, forming the foundation for enterprise adoption and long-term usage.

3. Carrier & Partner Onboarding

   CPaaS platforms establish connectivity with domestic and international telecom carriers, OTT messaging providers, email
   gateways, and cloud partners. This stage includes partner Selection, Contract Negotiation, API integration, and Compliance
   Validation. Strong carrier and partner relationships ensure global reach, high throughput, redundancy, and operational
   reliability, directly impacting platform economics, delivery rates, and enterprise-grade service quality.


                                                                124
4. Service Deployment & Campaign Configuration

     Following integration, providers configure client-specific workflows, including messaging flows, voice routing, AI bot
     deployment, and multi-agent orchestration. Campaign templates, message personalization, event triggers, and analytics
     tracking are established. This stage translates platform capabilities into actionable services, driving adoption, customer
     satisfaction, and usage-based revenue generation.

5. Execution, Monitoring & Analytics

     The platform executes communications in real-time across channels. Monitoring includes message delivery, voice call quality,
     API response times, and workflow efficiency. Analytics dashboards provide insights on campaign performance, engagement
     metrics, and predictive recommendations. This stage ensures SLA compliance, operational excellence, and actionable
     intelligence for client campaigns, supporting upsell opportunities and platform stickiness.

6. Post-Deployment Support & Optimization

     Ongoing support encompasses technical troubleshooting, workflow adjustments, AI model retraining, system upgrades, and
     platform optimization. Subscription-based updates, premium support packages, and consulting services strengthen recurring
     revenue streams, customer retention, and enterprise relationships. Effective support enhances platform reliability and long-
     term client engagement.

7. End-User Engagement & Feedback Loop

     The final stage captures client and end-user insights on platform performance, feature gaps, integration challenges, and
     emerging use cases. Feedback drives R&D prioritization, new channel integration (emerging OTTs, RCS evolution), AI model
     training, and global expansion. Continuous feedback ensures platform evolution, service innovation, and sustained market
     leadership.

     CPaaS providers operate a dual-stream revenue model. Subscription and platform access fees account for approximately 25-
     30% of revenue, while usage-based pricing (per-message, per-call, or per-API transaction) contributes roughly 70-75%. This
     structure enables scalable, predictable economics, supporting gross margins typically between 60-75% due to the software-
     driven nature of the business and operational leverage across development, orchestration, and enterprise support functions.

4.    GLOBAL AND INDIAN INDUSTRY OUTLOOK

4.1 Global IT Industry- CPaaS

Communications Platform as a Service (“CPaaS”) refers to cloud-based platforms that enable enterprises and public institutions
to embed communication capabilities—such as messaging, voice, video, and omnichannel interactions—directly into their
applications through application programming interfaces (“APIs”). CPaaS allows organizations to deliver customer notifications
and other real-time interactions at scale without developing or maintaining proprietary communication infrastructure. Over time,
CPaaS has evolved from a utility-driven messaging layer into a core component of enterprise digital engagement and workflow
automation.

Global Market Outlook

The global CPaaS market is estimated at USD 32.76 billion in 2026 and is projected to expand to USD 324.91 billion by 2036,
registering a compound annual growth rate (“CAGR”) of 25.79 percent. This expansion reflects increasing enterprise digitisation,
rising adoption of application-based customer engagement models, and the integration of programmable communication into
business-critical processes across sectors such as financial services, e-commerce, healthcare, logistics, and public administration.

    Regional Dynamics

    Industry Evolution

    The global CPaaS industry has progressed through three broad phases of development:

                         Foundation Phase (2010–2016): Platforms primarily offered SMS and voice APIs, enabling basic application-embedded
                          communications. This phase established industry standards and developer-led adoption models.

                         Expansion Phase (2017–2022): CPaaS platforms expanded to support omnichannel communication, including WhatsApp
                          Business API, Rich Communication Services (“RCS”), email, and over-the-top (“OTT”) channels, enabling coordinated
                          customer engagement across multiple touchpoints. Industry consolidation accelerated during this phase through mergers and
                          acquisitions.

                         Intelligence Phase (2023 onwards): CPaaS platforms increasingly integrate artificial intelligence-based orchestration,
                          analytics, and automation, supporting intelligent routing, conversational interfaces, fraud mitigation, and real-time
                          performance insights. As a result, CPaaS has evolved into strategic enterprise infrastructure rather than a standalone
                          messaging service.

                          The global CPaaS market exhibits moderate concentration, with leading multinational platforms accounting for a significant
                          share of industry revenues. Major global participants include developer-focused API providers and enterprise-oriented
                          omnichannel platforms with extensive carrier interconnections and cloud integrations. While large players benefit from scale,
                          compliance capabilities, and global reach, the market remains fragmented at regional and niche-use-case levels.


                                                                                      126
Cross-Border Service Delivery and Trade Characteristics

CPaaS operates predominantly as a digitally delivered cross-border service. Platforms developed in one jurisdiction provide
communication services to customers globally through cloud infrastructure and international telecom carrier networks. Revenues
generated from overseas customers are typically classified as exports of IT-enabled services, subject to applicable data
localisation, privacy, and telecom interconnection regulations in destination markets. This operating model enables global
scalability while increasing regulatory and operational complexity.

Regulatory and Compliance Environment

Global CPaaS providers operate within a multi-jurisdictional regulatory landscape encompassing data protection, consent-based
communications, and telecom routing requirements. Compliance with data privacy frameworks, unsolicited communication
regulations, and lawful interception obligations is critical for platform continuity. The need to manage regulatory alignment
across multiple geographies creates structural entry barriers and favours established platforms with mature governance
frameworks, compliance systems, and carrier relationships.

Enterprise and Public Sector Applications

CPaaS is widely deployed across both private and public sectors. Enterprise applications include customer authentication,
transaction alerts, order and delivery notifications, and interactive customer engagement. Public sector use cases include citizen
communications, identity verification, service notifications, and emergency alert systems. The breadth and criticality of these
applications reinforce CPaaS as essential digital infrastructure supporting real-time communication at scale.

The global CPaaS industry represents a rapidly expanding segment of the IT services landscape, underpinned by scalable cross-
border delivery models and increasing enterprise reliance on programmable communication. While regulatory complexity and
compliance requirements remain key challenges, established platforms with global reach, robust governance frameworks, and
advanced technology capabilities are well positioned to capture sustained growth as CPaaS continues to embed itself within
enterprise and public digital ecosystems.

4.2 Indian CPaaS Industry

In the Indian context, CPaaS platforms primarily support enterprise messaging and related communication workflows, operating
within the regulated telecommunications framework and leveraging the same API-driven architecture described above. The
Indian CPaaS industry operates at the intersection of telecommunications infrastructure, enterprise software services, and
application-based digital delivery, with a predominant focus on high-volume, compliance-sensitive enterprise messaging use
cases.

Market Size and Growth Outlook

Based on current market size estimates, the Indian CPaaS industry is projected to expand from approximately USD 1.17 billion
in 2026 to USD 10.32 billion by 2036, representing a compound annual growth rate (“CAGR”) of 24.28 percent over the period.
Within the global CPaaS landscape, India constitutes a relatively small but rapidly expanding market, reflecting increasing
enterprise adoption of programmable communication solutions across regulated and high-volume use cases.

These estimates reflect the broadening scope of CPaaS offerings in India—from traditional enterprise messaging to integrated

enterprise and public sector implementations.

Telecom and Digital Infrastructure Context

India represents one of the largest telecommunications markets globally, supported by an extensive wireless subscriber base and
widespread mobile broadband adoption. As per data published by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (“TRAI”) and the
Department of Telecommunications (“DoT”), India had approximately 1.17 billion wireless subscribers as of Q3 FY2025, with
mobile services accounting for the predominant share of total subscriptions. Mobile broadband penetration, led primarily by 4G
services, underpins large-scale application-to-person (“A2P”) communication traffic across enterprise and government
platforms. The scale and resilience of telecom infrastructure enable high-volume enterprise messaging activity, which forms the
core operational layer of CPaaS services in India.

Enterprise Messaging Characteristics

Enterprise messaging in India is characterised by high-frequency, mission-critical communication use cases. Messaging traffic
is largely transactional in nature, including authentication messages, service alerts, and system-generated notifications across
digital platforms. Such communications require high delivery reliability, low latency, and strict adherence to regulatory and
consumer protection norms. TRAI-mandated compliance mechanisms govern message origination, routing, and delivery to
ensure traceability and accountability within the telecom ecosystem.

Sectoral Demand Profile

Demand for CPaaS and enterprise messaging services in India arises across multiple sectors, including banking, financial services
and insurance (“BFSI”), e-commerce and digital consumer platforms, government departments and public sector undertakings,
and other enterprise segments such as healthcare, utilities, logistics, and education. These sectors utilise CPaaS primarily for
authentication, service notifications, transaction alerts, and citizen or customer communications, typically characterised by
continuous volumes and compliance sensitivity.

The organised segment of the Indian CPaaS industry comprises platforms with pan-India telecom connectivity, regulatory
compliance capabilities, and enterprise integration infrastructure. Regulatory requirements governing commercial messaging
have contributed to increased formalisation of messaging traffic routed through registered platforms. Competition within the
organised segment is based on delivery performance, compliance robustness, platform reliability, and integration capabilities, as
monitored under TRAI quality-of-service frameworks.

Export Orientation

CPaaS services provided by Indian platforms to overseas customers fall within the broader classification of software and IT-
enabled services. The Reserve Bank of India (“RBI”) recognises software and IT-enabled service exports as a significant


                                                                128
component of India’s services exports, reflecting the country’s established position as a global technology services hub. Indian
CPaaS providers leverage this ecosystem to service international enterprise clients, particularly across emerging markets.

The Indian CPaaS and enterprise messaging industry is supported by large-scale telecommunications infrastructure, a rapidly
expanding application-driven digital ecosystem, and a formalised regulatory framework. Market size estimates indicate strong
long-term growth potential, with industry expansion aligned to enterprise digitisation, public sector digital service delivery, and
India’s broader software and IT-enabled services landscape. Regulatory oversight and infrastructure scale are expected to remain
central to industry structure and competitive dynamics.

5.   MARKET DYNAMICS

5.1 Key Growth Drivers

The Communications Platform as a Service (“CPaaS”) segment within the Indian IT industry is positioned for sustained growth,
supported by structural digitalisation trends, rapid adoption of API-driven architectures, and increasing regulatory and security
requirements around enterprise and public communication. Growth is driven by rising demand for programmable, omnichannel
communication across banking, e-commerce, public services, and consumer internet platforms, alongside a shift from siloed,
channel-specific tools to integrated, workflow-centric engagement platforms. The segment is also benefiting from a progressive
transition toward recurring, platform-led revenue models anchored in subscription and usage-based pricing.

The table below summarises the principal market drivers and their directional impact over near (1–2 years), medium (3–4 years),
and longer (5–7 years) horizons.Market Drivers and Impact Assessment

 2. Growth in digital payments, e-commerce and BFSI usage                             High            High             High

Detailed Explanation of Key Growth Drivers

1.   API-Led Digital Transformation and Cloud Adoption

Indian enterprises and public sector entities are accelerating adoption of cloud-native architectures and microservices, driving
the need for programmable communication capabilities that can be embedded directly into applications and workflows. CPaaS
platforms provide standardised APIs for messaging, voice, video, and identity verification, enabling faster deployment and
reduced time-to-market for digital products. This driver supports sustained growth across all horizons, as API-first design and
cloud migration remain core components of digital transformation roadmaps.

2.   Growth in Digital Payments, E-Commerce and BFSI Usage

The scaling of digital payments, online lending, neo-banking, e-commerce marketplaces, and subscription platforms has
significantly increased volumes of transactional and event-driven communication, including OTPs, alerts, confirmations, and
status updates. These use cases rely on reliable, low-latency, and compliant messaging and voice infrastructure, directly aligned
with CPaaS capabilities. As transaction volumes and user bases expand, this driver continues to support high growth in CPaaS
utilisation over the near, medium, and long term.

3.   Regulatory Focus on Secure and Compliant Communication

Strengthening regulatory frameworks around telecom usage, spam control, consent management, and data protection have
increased the need for organised, compliant communication platforms. Requirements such as template registration, consent
capture, audit trails, and authentication-focused messaging favour structured CPaaS providers that can embed compliance into
their platforms. This driver provides long-term visibility, as regulatory oversight continues to deepen across sectors including
BFSI, healthcare, and public services, and extends to both domestic and cross-border communication.

4.   Adoption of AI-Driven, Omnichannel Customer Engagement



                                                                 129
Enterprises are increasingly moving from single-channel, campaign-centric communication to integrated, omnichannel customer
journeys supported by AI-driven personalisation. CPaaS platforms that combine messaging, voice, chat apps, and email with AI
bots, analytics, and workflow orchestration are well placed to capture this shift. Adoption is particularly pronounced in consumer
internet, e-commerce, BFSI, and customer service-intensive industries, and is expected to intensify over the medium to long term
as AI tools mature and become more widely embedded in enterprise processes.

5.   Enterprise Shift to Recurring, Platform-Based IT Models

The broader IT industry trend towards subscription-based, platform-centric consumption models is reinforcing CPaaS adoption,
as enterprises seek to reduce fixed infrastructure costs and align spend with usage. CPaaS offerings that bundle APIs,
orchestration, analytics, and compliance into unified platforms support this transition and enable predictable, scalable cost
structures. Over the medium to long term, this shift enhances revenue visibility for providers and encourages deeper integration
of CPaaS into core enterprise systems.

6.   Expansion into Tier II/III Cities and SME Digitisation

Increasing digitisation among small and medium enterprises, regional financial institutions, local e-commerce platforms, and
government programmes outside major metros is expanding the addressable market for CPaaS solutions. Self-service
onboarding, pay-as-you-go pricing, and simplified APIs make CPaaS accessible to smaller users who previously relied on basic
bulk messaging providers. While initially a moderate contributor, this driver is expected to gain significance over the long term
as digital inclusion deepens and regional ecosystems mature.

5.2 Challenges

The Communications Platform as a Service (“CPaaS”) segment, while poised for strong growth, faces several structural and
operational challenges that influence platform adoption, revenue visibility, and long-term sustainability. The table below
summarises the principal challenges and their directional impact over the near (1–2 years), medium (3–4 years), and longer (5–
7 years) horizons.

Market Challenges and Impact Assessment

(All values represent directional impact based on industry estimates and qualitative analysis)

                              Key Challenges                                    1–2 Years         3–4 Years       5–7 Years
   1. Platform Reliability and SLA Adherence                                   High              High            Medium
   2. Regulatory and Compliance Complexity                                     High              High            High
   3. Data Privacy and Cybersecurity Risks                                     High              High            High
   4. Integration Complexity with Enterprise Systems                           Medium            High            High
Source – Infomerics Analytics & Research

Detailed Commentary on Key Challenges

1.   Platform Reliability and SLA Adherence

     CPaaS providers operate mission-critical communication platforms that must guarantee high uptime, low latency, and
     consistent performance across messaging, voice, video, and identity services. Failures or delays in message delivery, system
     downtime, or workflow errors can lead to client dissatisfaction, SLA penalties, and revenue loss. Maintaining operational
     reliability under high-volume traffic and peak usage periods remains a key near- and medium-term challenge.

2.   Regulatory and Compliance Complexity

     The CPaaS industry is subject to multiple regulatory frameworks governing messaging, consent management, spam control,
     identity verification, and data protection. In India, DLT/TRAI compliance frameworks dictate sender registration, message
     templates, and audit trails, while international clients may require adherence to GDPR, TCPA, CASL, or local telecom
     regulations. Compliance obligations are evolving rapidly, increasing operational complexity and cost, particularly for
     providers serving BFSI, healthcare, and public sector clients.

3.   Data Privacy and Cybersecurity Risks

     Handling sensitive customer data, OTPs, transactional alerts, and enterprise communications exposes CPaaS platforms to
     cybersecurity threats, including data breaches, fraud, and unauthorized access. Providers must implement robust encryption,
     tokenization, monitoring, and security audits. Failure to prevent or respond effectively to breaches can lead to reputational
     damage, regulatory penalties, and contract termination.

                                                                 130
4.   Integration Complexity with Enterprise Systems

     Enterprises increasingly demand seamless integration of CPaaS APIs with CRM, ERP, cloud platforms, and workflow
     management systems. Variation in legacy systems, custom enterprise workflows, and multi-geography deployments can
     complicate implementation, extend onboarding timelines, and require specialized consulting and technical support.
     Integration challenges influence adoption speed and platform stickiness.

5.   Customer Concentration and Usage Volatility

     Revenue for CPaaS providers is often concentrated among a limited number of large enterprises, BFSI institutions, e-
     commerce platforms, and public sector clients. Fluctuations in usage volumes, seasonal campaign intensity, or contract
     renegotiations can result in revenue volatility. Dependence on high-volume clients highlights the importance of client
     diversification and the development of recurring subscription-based revenue streams to stabilise growth.

6.   PESTEL ANALYSIS OF THE INDUSTRY

The Communications Platform as a Service (“CPaaS”) industry in India operates within a dynamic regulatory, technological,
and market ecosystem. The PESTLE analysis summarises key external factors influencing the Indian CPaaS industry.

broadband and telecommunications have supported the expansion of digital communication requirements across government,
BFSI, fintech, e-commerce and enterprise applications. At the same time, regulations relating to commercial communications,
data protection, consent management, authentication and communication traceability have increased compliance requirements
for CPaaS providers.

Policy and Regulatory Implications for the Industry

Government initiatives relating to digitalisation, digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence, digital payments, broadband
expansion and e-governance have expanded the underlying demand for enterprise, government and transactional
communications in India. Programmes and platforms associated with Digital India, AI adoption, UPI-led payment digitisation
and digital government service delivery have increased the scale of digital interactions across public administration, BFSI,
fintech, e-commerce and enterprise applications. The expansion of API-enabled digital services and high-speed connectivity
further supports the adoption of programmable messaging, voice, authentication and omnichannel communication capabilities.
At the same time, the regulatory environment for digital communications has become more structured. TRAI's commercial
communication framework and subsequent directions relating to sender registration, consent, SMS template governance, UCC
controls and dedicated numbering arrangements have increased requirements for communication traceability and compliance.
The introduction of pre-tagging requirements for SMS variables and the phased implementation of dedicated numbering series
further strengthen the ability of the regulatory framework to distinguish and monitor legitimate enterprise communications.

The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and Rules, 2025 have further strengthened the framework governing the
processing and protection of digital personal data. The framework requires organisations to establish appropriate processes for
consent, security safeguards, breach management and data-principal rights, while cross-border processing is subject to prescribed
restrictions. Sector-specific regulatory frameworks may impose additional requirements relating to data storage, processing,
security and localisation.

The regulatory environment therefore contributes both to industry demand and higher compliance requirements. CPaaS providers
increasingly require capabilities covering consent management, sender and template governance, authentication, data protection,
information security and communication traceability. These requirements may increase technology, infrastructure and
compliance costs; however, they also contribute to greater formalisation of the communications ecosystem and raise the
importance of reliable, compliant and scalable platforms for mission-critical enterprise and government communications.
Overall, the policy environment remains supportive of the continued digitisation of communications in India, while the regulatory
framework is expected to require CPaaS providers to continuously adapt their technology architecture, compliance processes
and data-governance practices in line with evolving telecommunications, digital-payment and data-protection requirements.

8.   TECHNOLOGY AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION

The Communications Platform as a Service (CPaaS) industry is undergoing rapid technological transformation, driven by rising
transaction volumes, regulatory complexity, real-time communication requirements, and enterprise demand for scalable, API-
driven digital infrastructure. Modern CPaaS platforms are evolving beyond basic messaging delivery into integrated
communication orchestration layers that combine cloud-native architecture, AI-driven automation, analytics, and compliance-
by-design frameworks. Technology adoption within CPaaS is therefore focused on improving delivery reliability, regulatory
adherence, latency performance, and lifecycle management across high-volume, mission-critical communication workflows.

1.   API-First Architecture and Platform Orchestration

     CPaaS platforms are built on API-first, microservices-based architectures that enable seamless integration with enterprise
     applications, government platforms, fintech systems, and digital service ecosystems. RESTful APIs allow enterprises to
     embed messaging, voice, email, and OTT communication directly into transaction flows, authentication processes, and
     customer engagement journeys. Modular architecture enables rapid scaling across channels and geographies while
     maintaining service continuity. API orchestration layers also support routing logic, failover mechanisms, and dynamic


                                                                   135
     channel selection, improving delivery reliability for time-sensitive communications. This architecture positions CPaaS
     platforms as foundational digital infrastructure rather than standalone communication tools.

2.   Cloud-Native Infrastructure and Elastic Scalability

     Cloud-native deployment enables CPaaS platforms to handle large-scale, variable communication volumes with high
     availability and low latency. Containerisation, auto-scaling, and distributed cloud infrastructure allow platforms to support
     peak loads during OTP spikes, promotional campaigns, and government notification events. India-hosted cloud
     environments are increasingly prioritised to meet data localisation and regulatory requirements. Cloud-native design also
     supports faster feature deployment, cost optimisation, and resilience through multi-zone redundancy. These capabilities are
     critical for supporting BFSI, government, and enterprise use cases that demand near-zero downtime.

3.   AI-Driven Communication Intelligence

     Artificial intelligence and machine learning are increasingly embedded across CPaaS platforms to enhance communication
     efficiency and user experience. AI-driven routing engines optimise message delivery based on carrier performance, time-of-
     day rules, and historical success rates. Natural language processing (NLP) enables conversational AI, voice bots, and
     multilingual chatbots for customer support and government helplines. Predictive analytics are used to identify delivery risks,
     detect anomalous traffic patterns, and improve spam filtering. AI capabilities improve engagement outcomes while reducing
     operational costs and manual intervention.

4.   Omnichannel Communication Enablement

     CPaaS platforms are evolving into omnichannel communication hubs supporting SMS, voice, email, WhatsApp, RCS, and
     app-based notifications through a unified interface. Channel abstraction allows enterprises to manage multiple
     communication modes through a single integration, simplifying development and compliance management. Omnichannel
     orchestration supports fallback logic, ensuring message delivery even when a primary channel fails. This capability is
     increasingly critical as enterprises diversify authentication and engagement channels in response to regulatory, cost, and
     customer preference considerations.

5.   Real-Time Analytics and Performance Monitoring

     Advanced analytics engines provide real-time visibility into delivery rates, latency, failure patterns, and channel performance
     across millions of transactions. Dashboards enable enterprises and CPaaS operators to monitor SLA adherence, campaign
     effectiveness, and regulatory compliance metrics. Event-level logging supports forensic analysis, dispute resolution, and
     audit readiness. Data-driven insights also inform pricing optimisation, capacity planning, and infrastructure investment
     decisions. Analytics-driven operations enhance platform reliability and support enterprise-grade service commitments.

6.   Automation of Compliance and Consent Management

     Digital compliance platforms are integral to CPaaS operations, particularly in regulated environments. Automated workflows
     manage sender registration, template approvals, consent capture, consent revocation, and audit trails in alignment with
     telecom and data protection regulations. Compliance-by-design reduces manual errors, improves regulatory responsiveness,
     and minimises service disruption risks. Centralised documentation and automated validation support faster onboarding of
     enterprise clients and smoother regulatory inspections. Compliance automation has become a core differentiator for
     organised CPaaS providers.

7.   Security Architecture and Data Protection Frameworks

     CPaaS platforms implement multi-layered security frameworks covering encryption, access controls, identity management,
     and continuous monitoring. Security-by-design principles are applied across data storage, message processing, and API
     access layers. India-hosted infrastructure supports data residency requirements for sensitive personal and transactional data.
     Regular audits, penetration testing, and security certifications strengthen trust among BFSI, government, and enterprise
     customers. Robust security architecture is essential for sustaining large-scale transactional communication volumes.

8.   Emerging Technologies and Next-Generation Capabilities

     Emerging technologies such as edge computing, network APIs, and real-time media processing are shaping the next phase
     of CPaaS evolution. Edge deployment enables ultra-low-latency messaging and voice use cases in sectors such as healthcare,
     logistics, and industrial operations. Network API exposure allows CPaaS platforms to access carrier-level capabilities,
     including quality-of-service controls and advanced authentication. As communication requirements become more contextual
     and real-time, these technologies prepare CPaaS platforms for future digital service mandates and evolving enterprise
     expectations.


                                                                  136
     Technology and digital transformation have positioned CPaaS platforms as critical digital infrastructure layers supporting
     high-frequency, regulated, and mission-critical communication workflows. Continuous investment in cloud-native
     architecture, AI-driven intelligence, omnichannel orchestration, compliance automation, and security frameworks enables
     CPaaS providers to scale reliably while meeting stringent regulatory and performance requirements. As enterprises and
     governments deepen their reliance on digital communication, technology-led CPaaS platforms are expected to play an
     increasingly central role in India’s digital economy ecosystem.

9.   COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE

The Communications Platform as a Service (CPaaS) industry in India operates within a multi-layered competitive environment
comprising global cloud communication providers, telecom-integrated platforms, regional aggregators, and application-focused
CPaaS specialists. Competitive intensity is driven less by pricing and more by platform reliability, regulatory compliance,
scalability, security architecture, and the ability to support high-volume, mission-critical enterprise communication workflows.
As enterprise adoption deepens across BFSI, e-commerce, healthcare, logistics, and government services, differentiation
increasingly hinges on compliance maturity, delivery assurance, and long-term platform integration rather than transactional
messaging volumes.

9.1 Key Factors Shaping Competition

Competition in the CPaaS industry is driven by the ability to deliver secure, compliant, and scalable communication infrastructure
within a complex telecom and data protection environment. Market participants differentiate through platform reliability,
regulatory readiness, integration depth, vertical relevance, and long-term client engagement, rather than pricing or message
volumes alone.

1.   Platform Reliability and Uptime Assurance

     Enterprise communication use cases increasingly require near-continuous availability for transactional alerts, authentication,
     customer engagement, and service notifications. Providers with resilient cloud architecture, multi-operator routing, and built-
     in failover mechanisms are preferred, particularly in regulated and mission-critical segments such as banking, payments,
     healthcare, and government services.

2.   Regulatory and Telecom Compliance Capability

     Adherence to TRAI regulations, spam control frameworks, customer consent requirements, and evolving data protection
     obligations is a core competitive determinant. CPaaS providers with embedded compliance workflows, audit-ready reporting
     systems, and active regulatory monitoring are better positioned to onboard large enterprises and institutional clients with
     stringent governance requirements.

3.   Scalability and Traffic Management

     The ability to manage high-volume and peak-load communication traffic—especially during campaigns, seasonal spikes, or
     transaction surges—constitutes a key differentiator. Platforms demonstrating elastic scaling, intelligent queue management,
     and throughput stability are favoured for enterprise-wide deployments and mission-critical communication flows.

4.   API Depth and Developer Ecosystem

     Comprehensive APIs, SDKs, and integration frameworks enable faster enterprise onboarding and deeper system embedding.
     CPaaS platforms that integrate seamlessly with CRM, ERP, payment, and identity systems achieve higher operational
     dependency, increased switching costs, and stronger long-term client retention.

5.   Security Architecture and Data Protection

     Handling of sensitive personal and transactional data places security at the centre of competitive positioning. Providers with
     strong encryption standards, access controls, monitoring frameworks, and incident response mechanisms—aligned with data
     localization and enterprise security expectations—gain credibility with regulated and compliance-driven customers.

6.   Vertical-Specific Solution Capability

     Industry-aligned communication workflows for BFSI, e-commerce, logistics, healthcare, and public services enhance
     platform differentiation. Providers offering pre-configured, compliance-aligned messaging templates and sector-specific
     reporting frameworks achieve faster adoption and deeper integration within client operations.



                                                                  137
7.   Lifecycle Client Engagement Model

     Beyond message delivery, competitive advantage increasingly stems from the ability to support clients across onboarding,
     optimisation, compliance updates, analytics, and platform evolution. CPaaS providers with consultative engagement and
     lifecycle support models demonstrate higher client retention and sustained revenue expansion.

9.2 Competitive Strategies

CPaaS providers deploy targeted strategies to sustain growth in a compliance-intensive, technology-driven operating
environment. Successful platforms balance continuous innovation with regulatory discipline, while aligning infrastructure
investments, product design, and go-to-market models with evolving enterprise communication requirements.

1.   Compliance-First Platform Design

     Leading CPaaS providers architect compliance as a core platform feature rather than a post-deployment overlay. Consent
     management, sender and template controls, audit logs, and real-time regulatory reporting are embedded directly into message
     workflows. This approach reduces compliance burden and operational risk for enterprise clients, positioning the platform as
     a trusted, regulation-aligned communication backbone rather than a commodity messaging layer.

2.   Infrastructure-Led Differentiation

     Providers invest in resilient cloud architecture, multi-operator connectivity, geographic redundancy, and intelligent traffic
     routing to ensure consistent delivery performance. Infrastructure depth enables platforms to support high-criticality use cases
     such as authentication, financial alerts, and service notifications at scale. Strong infrastructure capability also underpins the
     ability to service large, long-tenure enterprise contracts with stringent uptime and latency expectations.

3.   Enterprise Integration and Platform Stickiness

     Strategic focus is placed on deep integration with enterprise systems such as CRM, ERP, payment gateways, identity
     platforms, and customer support tools. Tight system embedding enables CPaaS services to become integral to core business
     processes, increasing switching costs and shifting client relationships from usage-based engagement to long-term platform
     partnerships.

4.   Vertical Expansion Strategy

     CPaaS providers increasingly prioritise high-value, compliance-sensitive verticals such as BFSI, fintech, e-commerce,
     healthcare, logistics, and government services. Vertical specialisation allows platforms to develop domain-specific
     workflows, regulatory familiarity, and reference deployments. This reduces solution commoditisation, improves execution
     reliability, and strengthens credibility in institutional procurement processes.

5.   Security and Trust Positioning

     As CPaaS platforms handle sensitive personal and transactional data, providers strengthen their security posture through
     robust encryption, access controls, monitoring frameworks, and governance processes. Security certifications, transparent
     policies, and incident-response readiness enhance trust among regulated enterprises, where vendor credibility and risk
     management are central to procurement decisions.

6.   Partner and Ecosystem Development

     Strategic alliances with telecom operators, cloud infrastructure providers, system integrators, and application vendors extend
     market reach and solution completeness. Ecosystem partnerships enable faster enterprise deployments, improved
     interoperability, and bundled solution offerings, supporting participation in large-scale digital transformation initiatives.

7.   Geographic and Regulatory Expansion

     Providers pursue measured geographic expansion by aligning platform capabilities with local telecom regulations, data
     protection laws, and operational requirements. Regulatory adaptability and modular platform design enable sustainable
     expansion while minimising compliance risk, operational disruption, and reputational exposure in new markets.

9.3 Barriers to Entry

The Indian CPaaS industry demonstrates high structural and operational entry barriers, particularly for platforms targeting
enterprise, BFSI, fintech, healthcare, and government segments. Market participation increasingly favours providers with proven


                                                                   138
infrastructure, compliance maturity, operational credibility, and domain-specific expertise. New entrants face a combination of
regulatory, technical, and commercial hurdles that extend beyond simple capital investment.

1.   Telecom and Regulatory Complexity

     New platforms must navigate a multilayered regulatory environment including TRAI messaging and consent frameworks,
     TCCCPR compliance, DLT registration, and evolving data protection obligations under the DPDP Act. Enterprises
     increasingly demand audit-ready, regulation-compliant communication channels, which imposes a steep learning curve and
     high operational risk for entrants unfamiliar with India-specific norms.

2.   Infrastructure Investment Requirements

     Delivering enterprise-grade CPaaS necessitates significant investment in resilient cloud architecture, multi-operator routing,
     failover systems, traffic orchestration, and monitoring frameworks. Platforms must be capable of sustaining high-volume,
     low-latency transactional workloads such as OTPs, payment alerts, and critical service notifications. Underinvestment in
     these areas results in unreliable delivery and client attrition.

3.   Trust and Enterprise Credibility

     Large enterprises prioritise platforms with a track record of consistent delivery, regulatory adherence, and security
     governance. Establishing credibility requires referenceable deployments, operational transparency, and demonstrable risk
     management. New entrants without such proof points face a long gestation period before winning contracts in regulated
     sectors.

4.   Security and Data Protection Obligations

     Handling sensitive personal and financial data necessitates robust encryption, access controls, continuous monitoring, audits,
     and compliance-aligned governance frameworks. Non-compliance or operational lapses carry not only regulatory penalties
     but also reputational damage, making security a critical barrier to entry for smaller or under-resourced platforms.

5.   Integration and Ecosystem Dependencies

     Effective CPaaS delivery depends on deep technical and commercial integrations with telecom operators, aggregators, cloud
     infrastructure providers, and enterprise systems. Established players benefit from long-standing vendor relationships,
     preferential routing agreements, and proven interoperability, which new entrants must replicate at scale to achieve
     comparable reliability and reach.

6.   Talent and Operational Expertise

     Operating large-scale CPaaS platforms requires specialised expertise in telecom operations, cloud architecture, software
     development, compliance, and enterprise support. The scarcity of such talent in combination with the steep operational
     learning curve limits the ability of inexperienced entrants to scale quickly while maintaining enterprise-grade service levels.

7.   Customer and Market Stickiness

     Enterprise clients exhibit high switching costs due to integration, compliance alignment, and operational continuity
     requirements. Established CPaaS providers benefit from long-term engagements and recurring transaction volumes, creating
     a natural moat that discourages new competitors from entering high-value segments without significant upfront investment
     and proof of capability.

9.4 Consolidation Trends

The Indian CPaaS industry is undergoing gradual and selective consolidation, driven by rising compliance expectations,
infrastructure scale advantages, and enterprise preference for reliable, long-term communication partners. Consolidation is
increasingly capability-led, favouring platforms that combine regulatory expertise, secure infrastructure, and enterprise-grade
service delivery. Smaller, niche providers continue to operate in specialised or transactional segments, while larger, organised
platforms capture mission-critical workloads.

1.   Shift Toward Organised Platforms

     Enterprise clients and regulated sectors such as BFSI, fintech, healthcare, and government increasingly prioritise providers
     with demonstrable compliance, security, and uptime performance. This preference concentrates demand among established
     platforms that can consistently deliver high-volume, low-latency communication across multi-channel enterprise workflows.


                                                                  139
2.   Capability-Driven Consolidation

     Leading CPaaS providers are strengthening their market position by integrating complementary capabilities, including AI-
     driven analytics, real-time authentication APIs, fraud detection, and security services. Such consolidation enables end-to-
     end enterprise communication solutions, reducing dependency on fragmented vendors and enhancing client stickiness.

3.   Rising Procurement Thresholds

     Enterprise and institutional procurement increasingly mandates robust technical, security, and compliance credentials,
     including audit-ready systems, data localisation, consent frameworks, and scalable cloud architecture. These heightened
     requirements narrow the pool of eligible vendors, reinforcing the dominance of infrastructure-backed, compliance-mature
     platforms.

4.   Strategic Alliances Over Pure M&A

     Mid-scale and regional CPaaS providers often prefer partnerships, API integrations, and ecosystem collaborations over
     balance-sheet-heavy acquisitions. Strategic alliances with cloud providers, telcos, system integrators, and application
     vendors expand service reach, accelerate go-to-market execution, and enable capability aggregation without heavy capital
     deployment.

5.   Long-Term Client Relationships

     Repeat contracts, embedded enterprise integrations, and consultative engagement models reinforce consolidation by
     favouring incumbents with proven performance, regulatory reliability, and operational continuity. Platform lock-in and
     embedded workflow adoption further reduce the competitive threat from newer entrants.

6.   Overall Assessment

     Consolidation in the CPaaS industry is selective, structural, and capability-driven, resulting in increasing concentration of
     enterprise and compliance-sensitive communication workloads among organised, infrastructure-backed platforms. Smaller
     providers continue to serve niche or transactional segments, but large-scale, regulated, and mission-critical workloads are
     increasingly dominated by mature players with integrated platforms, security certifications, and regulatory alignment.

     The CPaaS industry in India is transitioning from volume-driven messaging models to enterprise-grade, compliance-centric
     communication platforms. Competitive advantage is increasingly anchored in platform reliability, regulatory alignment,
     security architecture, and deep enterprise integration, rather than pricing alone. Growth opportunities remain strong across
     digital commerce, financial services, government e-governance, and large-scale fintech operations. However, sustained
     success depends on compliance maturity, platform resilience, operational credibility, and trust-based client relationships.
     Providers that combine technological scale with regulatory discipline are best positioned to capture long-term value, as
     CPaaS evolves into a core digital utility for enterprise and mission-critical communication infrastructure.

9.5 Key Industry Players

The Communications Platform as a Service ("CPaaS") industry in India comprises a spectrum of organised entities operating
across the digital communication value chain. This landscape includes global hyperscalers providing programmable
communication APIs, telco-integrated platforms leveraging network assets, India-headquartered pure-play CPaaS providers
focused on compliance and enterprise messaging, and specialised application platforms. These participants enable enterprise
digital transformation, financial services digitisation, e-governance, and high-volume customer engagement across BFSI, e-
commerce, government services, and digital-first enterprises. Key industry participants include Tanla Platforms Limited and
Route Mobile Limited. Brief profiles of these entities are set out below.

    Tanla Platforms Limited

     Tanla Platforms Limited, incorporated on July 26, 1999 and headquartered in Hyderabad, Telangana, is India’s leading A2P
     messaging platform and a global player in cloud communications, processing high-volume enterprise messages for thousands
     of clients worldwide. The company delivers mission-critical communication infrastructure through its Trubloq platform,
     pioneering AI-powered anti-phishing and enterprise messaging solutions.

     Tanla’s core offerings include Trubloq, an AI-native communication platform integrating Users.ai (user protection) and
     Enterprise.ai (enterprise engagement), featuring end-to-end encryption, DLT/TRAI compliance, and zero-trust security. Its
     Wisely ATP platform provides AI/ML-based SMS anti-phishing with patent-pending engines to prevent phishing at source.
     The company also offers omnichannel communication through SMS, WhatsApp Business, RCS, Google Business Messages,


                                                                 140
    email, and voice, augmented by rich media and conversational AI. Additionally, Tanla provides anti-fraud solutions,
    including real-time scam detection, number intelligence, and behavioural analytics to protect BFSI and digital-native
    enterprises.

    Strategic differentiators for Tanla include AI-first platform architecture, TRAI DLT 2.0 and DPDP Act compliance, SOC2
    and ISO 27001 certification, scalable infrastructure supporting mission-critical workflows, and strong partnerships with
    government and enterprise clients. Tanla Platforms exemplifies enterprise-grade CPaaS leadership, combining AI
    innovation, compliance maturity, scalable infrastructure, and mission-critical reliability to support India’s digital
    communication ecosystem.

   Route Mobile Limited

    Route Mobile Limited, incorporated on March 20, 2004 and headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, is a global CPaaS
    provider operating a proprietary super-network connecting hundreds of telecom operators across multiple countries and
    languages. The company delivers scalable, compliant cloud communication services to thousands of enterprise clients,
    supporting mission-critical transactional and engagement workflows.

    Route Mobile’s core offerings include Route OCEAN, a unified CPaaS platform integrating SMS, Voice, WhatsApp
    Business API, RCS, Viber, Email, OTT messaging, and rich media communications. The company also provides Enhanced
    Business Messaging (EBM) through interactive formats on WhatsApp, RCS, Google Business Messages, and Viber, Route
    Shield Firewall for A2P traffic intelligence and fraud detection, and Identity & Authentication solutions including OTP
    delivery, number masking, verification APIs, KYC compliance, and fraud prevention. Its Enterprise APIs enable low-latency
    REST API, SMPP, webhooks, and SDK integration with CRM/ERP systems.

    Strategic differentiators for Route Mobile include an extensive super-network with multi-route redundancy, TRAI DLT 2.0
    compliance, ISO 27001 and SOC2 certification, GDPR/TCPA readiness, omnichannel messaging capabilities, and AI-
    powered analytics for operational and telco revenue optimisation. Route Mobile exemplifies global-scale CPaaS leadership,
    combining carrier connectivity, enterprise-grade reliability, omnichannel depth, and regulatory compliance to deliver
    mission-critical communication solutions across India and international markets.

    These industry participants illustrate the organised segment of India’s CPaaS ecosystem. Tanla Platforms Limited focuses
    on AI-driven enterprise messaging and anti-fraud solutions for BFSI, technology, and government sectors, while Route
    Mobile Limited provides a globally distributed, omnichannel CPaaS platform with extensive carrier connectivity and
    enterprise integrations. Together, these leaders demonstrate platform scalability, compliance maturity, innovation, and
    mission-critical delivery across India’s digital communication infrastructure.

9.6 Company Positioning

Dove Soft Limited (the “Company”), headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, is engaged in the provision of cloud-based
communication platform as a service (“CPaaS”) solution, enabling enterprises and public sector institutions to manage and
automate customer communications across multiple digital and voice-based channels. Incorporated in 2011, the Company
operates a technology-led, platform-driven business model focused on omnichannel customer engagement and enterprise
messaging solutions.

Over time, the Company has evolved from a messaging-centric service provider into an integrated CPaaS platform offering,
supporting customer interactions across the full lifecycle, including marketing communication, authentication and verification,
service delivery, customer support and post-purchase engagement. The Company’s offerings are designed to be deployed through
application programming interfaces (“APIs”) and system integrations, allowing customers to embed communication capabilities
within their internal applications and business workflows.

The Company’s solution portfolio comprises SMS and OTP messaging, Rich Communication Services (“RCS”), WhatsApp
Business API solutions, voice and AI-enabled voice bots, enterprise email communication tools, and mobile identity verification
services through its Sekura.id platform. These solutions support transactional, promotional, service and automation-led use cases
and are deployed across a range of enterprise and institutional requirements.

The Company operates an omnichannel platform architecture that integrates multiple engagement channels, including
messaging, voice and email, with an intelligence layer comprising analytics, campaign management tools, workflow
orchestration and integrations with third-party customer relationship management, e-commerce and enterprise software
platforms. This architecture enables enterprises to centralise communication workflows, monitor engagement performance and
manage customer interactions through a unified platform.

Dove Soft services a diversified customer base across private enterprises and public sector institutions. Its customers operate
across sectors such as media and entertainment, retail and consumer goods, automotive, manufacturing, banking and financial
services, and government-backed institutions. This sectoral diversification supports demand across both consumer-facing
communication use cases and compliance-driven enterprise messaging requirements.

The Company conducts its operations through offices located in Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Gurugram and Dubai, supporting
domestic and international customer engagement. Its global operating presence is further supported through its subsidiary,
Dovesoft Tech, which extends the Company’s reach across additional geographies and enterprise segments.

The Company follows an asset-light, cloud-native operating model, with core activities centred on platform development,
product management, enterprise integration, compliance oversight and customer support. Service delivery is enabled through
internal technical and engineering teams, supported by partnerships with telecommunications carriers and cloud infrastructure
providers. This operating structure allows scalability while limiting capital intensity and fixed asset ownership.

The Company’s solutions are positioned to support enterprises across the entire customer engagement lifecycle, including
customer acquisition, pre-purchase communication, identity verification, service automation, transactional messaging, and post-
purchase engagement and personalisation. This end-to-end positioning enables enterprises to consolidate multi-channel
communication requirements within a single platform.

Through its integrated CPaaS offerings, omnichannel platform architecture, diversified customer base, multi-geographic
presence and asset-light operating model, Dove Soft Limited is positioned as a provider of scalable digital communication and
customer engagement solutions catering to evolving enterprise and institutional communication requirements.

10. FUTURE OUTLOOK

The Communications Platform as a Service (CPaaS) industry in India is expected to witness strong structural growth over the
medium to long term, supported by continued enterprise digitisation, increasing reliance on API-driven communication
workflows, and rising demand for real-time, secure, and compliant customer engagement solutions. CPaaS platforms enable
enterprises to integrate messaging, voice, authentication, notifications, and other communication functionalities directly into
business applications, thereby supporting scalability, automation, and operational efficiency across industries.

The Indian CPaaS market is projected to expand from INR 1.17 lakh crore in 2026E to INR 10.32 lakh crore by 2036P, registering
a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.28% over the period. The projected growth is expected to be driven by increasing
adoption across banking, financial services and insurance, e-commerce, logistics, healthcare, government services, and digital-
first enterprises, where high-volume, time-critical, and compliant communication has become integral to core operations.

Structural demand drivers include the continued shift toward digital customer journeys, rising usage of application-to-person
(A2P) messaging and authentication, expansion of cloud-native enterprise platforms, and growing reliance on automated alerts,
notifications, and conversational interfaces. Increasing smartphone penetration and rising acceptance of digital interactions
among consumers are expected to further support sustained demand for CPaaS solutions across both large enterprises and mid-
market customers.

The industry is also experiencing a gradual technology-led evolution, with CPaaS platforms increasingly incorporating advanced
analytics and automation capabilities to enhance delivery performance, engagement effectiveness, and operational monitoring.
Integration of communication APIs with enterprise systems such as customer relationship management platforms and internal
workflow tools is expected to deepen platform embedment and increase switching costs, thereby supporting longer customer
relationships.

Regulatory and ecosystem developments are expected to continue shaping industry dynamics. India’s regulated telecom
framework, including requirements related to consent management, message traceability, and template registration, has led to
greater formalisation of enterprise messaging traffic. This environment is expected to favour CPaaS platforms with established
compliance capabilities, scalable infrastructure, and operational reliability, as enterprises increasingly prioritise regulatory
adherence and delivery assurance.

From a commercial perspective, the CPaaS industry benefits from recurring usage-based revenue models, expanding use cases
per customer, and long-term enterprise relationships. As enterprises scale communication volumes and diversify channels, CPaaS
platforms are expected to capture increasing share of customer communication spend, supporting revenue visibility and operating
leverage over time.

The Indian CPaaS industry is entering a high-growth phase, underpinned by strong enterprise demand, regulatory formalisation,
and continued digital transformation across sectors. With the market projected to grow at a CAGR of 24.28% between 2026 and
2036, CPaaS is expected to remain a critical component of enterprise digital infrastructure. Companies with scalable platforms,
strong compliance frameworks, and deep enterprise integration capabilities are expected to be well positioned to benefit from
the industry’s long-term growth trajectory.

Business Overview

Our Company was originally incorporated as private limited Company under the name “Dove Soft Private Limited”, under
the provisions of the Companies Act, 1956 and Certificate of Incorporation was issued by the Registrar of Companies,
Maharashtra, Mumbai on August 19, 2011. Subsequently, our Company was converted into a public limited company
pursuant to shareholder’s resolution passed at the general meeting of our Company held on August 17, 2022, and the name
of our Company was changed to “Dove Soft Limited” and a fresh certificate of incorporation dated September 19, 2022,
was issued by the Registrar of Companies, Mumbai. The Corporate Identification Number of our Company is
U74900MH2011PLC221087. For details of change in registered office of our Company, please refer to chapter titled
“History and Certain Corporate Matters” beginning on page no. 181.

Our Company is an integrated provider of cloud communications solutions in India. commonly known as a CPaaS
(Communications Platform as a Service) provider. We offer a wide range of services through channels such as SMS, RCS,
Voice, WhatsApp, Email, and other digital platforms. Our solutions enable businesses to communicate efficiently with their
customers through reliable and scalable messaging and engagement tools.

We provide services to enterprises as well as over-the-top (OTT) platforms, including transactional SMS, WhatsApp
messaging solutions, voice services, automated voice call solutions, email communication, and various digital products.

Our organization acts as an aggregator between telecom operators and clients, ensuring seamless connectivity and delivery
of communication services.

We serve clients across multiple industries, including Telecom, Information Technology, Travel & Tourism, Entertainment,
Media, Advertising & Events, Retail, Real Estate, Healthcare & Cosmetics, Banking, Financial Services & Insurance
(BFSI), Automobile, E-commerce, and Food & Beverages. Our solutions help businesses effectively manage customer
communication, enhance engagement, and streamline their operational processes.

Our sales team actively engages with existing and potential clients to promote our range of communication solutions. By
understanding each client’s marketing objectives and business requirements, we present the most suitable services from our
existing portfolio.

Based on the client’s specific needs, we design and propose a customized communication plan. Once the client approves
the proposed strategy, our team proceeds with the implementation and execution of the plan to ensure effective delivery of
services.

We are committed to delivering quality solutions that support our clients in achieving their business goals and maintaining
efficient customer communication. Our organization is supported by a dedicated team of skilled technicians and
professionals who ensure reliable service delivery and technical excellence.

The Company has two subsidiary entities, namely Dove Soft Technologies Private Limited and Dove Soft Global FZCO.

BRIEF DETAILS OF OUR BUSINESS SERVICES:

Our operations are internally aligned into the following business services:




                                                               149
1. SMS:

    Transactional SMS & OTP SMS

Transactional SMS is a type of SMS sent to customers to share important information related to their account, services, or
transactions. These messages are typically non-promotional, time-sensitive, and informative.

Operational Scenarios for Transactional SMS-

 Order & Delivery Updates
    Your order #12345 has been shipped and will be delivered by April 12.

 Booking Confirmations
    Your flight booking (PNR: A1B2C3) is confirmed for April 15 at 10:30 AM.

 Account Notifications
    Your monthly bank statement is now available. Login to your account to view it.

 Appointment Reminders
    Reminder: Your appointment with Dr. Smith is scheduled for April 13 at 2:00 PM.

 Policy/Renewal Alerts
    Your car insurance policy will expire on April 20. Please renew to stay covered.

OTP (One-Time Password) SMS is used to verify user identity during online transactions, registrations, or logins. These
messages contain short-lived passcodes and are crucial for secure authentication.

Operational Scenarios for OTP SMS-

    User Login Verification
     Your OTP for login is 928374. It will expire in 5 minutes.

    Transaction Approval
     To authorize your fund transfer of ₹50,000, use OTP 472819.

    New Device or Location Login
     New login attempt detected. Enter OTP 624389 to confirm it’s you.

    Account Signup Verification
     Welcome! Use OTP 183920 to verify your mobile number and complete registration.


                                                              150
    Password Reset Authentication
     Reset your password with this OTP: 590237. Valid for 10 minutes.

   Campaign Management

Campaigning management is a process of organising and running each step of campaign from planning to execution.
Effective campaign management tools are integral to successful campaign execution for companies globally. Whether one
operates with a compact or expansive team, leveraging these tools is paramount for accelerating productivity and
streamlining your daily operations.

For instance, a retail brand is planning to run a customer engagement campaign across India using mobile messaging
channels to promote an upcoming seasonal sale. The brand already possesses a robust customer database segmented by
region, purchase behaviour, and communication preferences.

This campaign involves multiple components such as designing tailored message content for SMS, WhatsApp, Rich
Communication Services (“RCS”), and Voice; setting up personalized targeting based on user preferences; defining fallback
rules (e.g., using SMS if RCS is not supported); and scheduling delivery timings for optimal engagement.

In addition, the campaign includes performance tracking, link click monitoring, and customer response collection to refine
future outreach.

2. Voice

The Wholesale Voice Service offers voice technologies, enabling enterprises and operators to engage in global phone calls
and integrate advanced voice features like text-to-speech, conferencing, recording, and transcription. Our extensive solution
portfolio offers international wholesale voice-over-internet-protocol termination services as well as enterprise voice
solutions. Leveraging our platform and APIs, both enterprises and operators can cater to their needs for contact centres, call
tracking, analytics solutions, and seamless communications. Our wholesale voice service seamlessly operates over both
traditional public switched telephone networks and internet protocols.

   Missed Call

The missed call service serves as an engagement tool, allowing customers to provide inbound inputs through a
straightforward and cost-free phone call. This tool can be deployed to gather responses or address inquiries, sending
automated messages or scheduling calls with customers accordingly.

The missed call service operates by publishing a virtual mobile number across diverse mediums like billboards, banners,
or promotional messages. When a customer dials the number, the call is redirected to our server and is subsequently
disconnected. The caller’s information is recorded in our systems. Following this, an automated response is promptly
dispatched to the customer in the form of a text message.

Automated Voice Call

                                      The Automated Voice facility allows enterprises to automatically make calls to pre-
                                      defined customer lists and deliver one-time passwords, promotional messages, or
                                      reminders in accordance with their specific needs.

                                      The message for broadcasting is generated and uploaded as an audio file,
                                      accompanied by a list of phone numbers. Our system then autonomously dials the
                                      provided numbers and plays the recorded audio. Call statuses are updated in the
                                      database. For any calls that receive no response, the system automatically redials at
                                      designated intervals within a specified timeframe. The Automated Voice Call
                                      empowers enterprises to access reports on the voice panel, offering insights into total
                                      calls, successful calls, failed calls, and calls with no response.

    to onboard and manage thousands of outlets, dealers, branches, and franchise locations from a single interface, ensuring
    consistent and accurate Name–Address–Phone (NAP) details, categories, business hours, photos, and attributes across

    platforms. It is designed for industries with distributed networks such as retail, BFSI, healthcare, automotive, quick
    service restaurants, and telecom.

These AI capabilities are embedded directly into the operational workflows of Map My Business, enabling enterprises to
manage large location footprints efficiently while enhancing the quality and consistency of their local digital presence

Key Benefits:

     Bing, and Apple Maps, reducing operational overhead and manual errors.

Process Flow:

1. SMS:


    DLT Registration             SMS Types                 User                    SMS                   Delivery
                                and Delivery            Onboarding               Submission             Report & UI
     Requirements                  Rules                and Access               Workflow                Features


    Distributed Ledger Technology (“DLT”) Registration Requirements:

For sending SMS through our platform, the clients must first register their business entity on the Distributed Ledger
Technology (“DLT”) portal. Additionally, they need to register their SMS templates and Sender IDs to comply with TRAI
regulations.

    SMS Types and Delivery Rules

The clients are required to select either the Transactional SMS option or the OTP SMS option. Transactional SMS messages
are utilized by businesses to disseminate essential information, including but not limited to order status updates and account
notifications. OTP SMS messages, by contrast, are intended solely for authentication purposes and are designed to be
delivered instantaneously to facilitate secure user verification.

    User Onboarding and Access

Dove Soft creates an account for the client in its proprietary web application. Customers can log into the User Interface
(“UI”) to send SMS or use Application Programming Interface (“API”) and short message peer-to-peer protocol (“SMPP”)
protocol for integration with their existing systems.

    SMS Submission Workflow

Once validated, our system stores the SMS content, recipient’s mobile number, and other essential details in a database.
We use a separate backend module named ‘SMPP Engine’ to submit messages to telecom operators. The SMPP Engine
fetches the data from the database and submits it to the operator as per the configured routing. Once the operator processes
the SMS, a Delivery Report (“DLR”) is returned and stored in our system.


                                                               154
      Delivery Report & UI Features

Our user interface, mobiCOMM, presents detailed delivery reports including:

      Day-wise summary
      Month-wise summary
      Error- reason wise summary
      Delivery timing in seconds

Clients can also download detailed logs and use advanced features such as scheduling SMS, masking content or numbers
for added privacy.

      Client Onboarding and Dashboard Access

Upon successful completion of the Know Your Customer (“KYC”) process and business verification in accordance with
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (“TRAI”) guidelines, the Client will be onboarded to the Platform. A dedicated,
fully white-labelled dashboard will be provisioned for the Client, with identity verification completed for all voice-related
services. The Client shall be granted role-based access to various dashboard types (e.g., Administrator, Agent, Campaign
Manager), each of which includes multi-tiered access controls. The dashboard enables access to core functionalities
including campaign creation, call logs, contact management, and real-time analytics.

      Number Allocation & Caller Identification Configuration

The Client shall be assigned a Private Caller Identifications for the purpose of brand representation and call recognition.
Custom voice numbers, including Direct Inward Dialling (DID) numbers, may be allocated and mapped to specific
campaigns, departments, or use cases as determined by the Client.

      Service Type Selection

Following        onboarding,       the         Client   shall      select      the    desired     voice   service(s),   which   may    include:

a) Automated Voice Broadcast- Allows scheduling of high-volume campaigns delivering pre-recorded or TTS-generated
   voice messages to mobile and landline numbers, either via API HTTP/HTTPS using JSON payloads) or through the
   dashboard UI.
b) Missed Call Services- Assigns unique missed call numbers to campaigns for lead capture. Upon receiving a missed
   call, the system automatically captures the caller’s number, sends a confirmation message, updates the Client’s CRM,
   and initiates follow-up actions through webhooks or agent callbacks.

      Voice Content Upload and Configuration

The Client may upload pre-recorded voice files or utilize Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities to generate dynamic messages.
The system supports variable insertion (e.g., customer name, one-time password, balance) and configure keypress detection
(e.g., “Press 1 to express interest,” “Press 9 to unsubscribe”) to enhance interactivity.

      API Integration

The client uses our HTTP/HTTPS API enabling the Clients to schedule campaigns, push contacts, pull reports, and trigger
outbound voice calls directly from Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems or business workflow engines.

      Webhook and Call Routing Configuration

The Client may configure webhooks to transmit event-level data—including call responses, keypress actions, and call
logs—in real-time. Workflow automation features enable the system to dynamically assign leads or route calls based on
keypress inputs, campaign metadata, or predefined business logic.

      Real-Time Monitoring & Reports

                                                                                  155
The Platform provides real-time visibility into campaign performance metrics including call success/failure rates, pickup
ratios, keypress analytics, and engagement summaries. Reports are available in multiple formats and may include (but are
not limited to):

    Campaign Performance Summary
    API Usage and Log Reports
    Keypress Interaction Analytics
    Call Duration and Disposition Reports

      Client onboarding & WhatsApp Business Profile set up
